answer: Draw rotating committees so any two overlap by only a small delta of members. A farm whose clones share one island of infrastructure then cannot fill a quorum: random assignment acts as a prism, scattering its aliases into rooms where honest outsiders still outnumber them. To sway one decision the attacker must seed many committees at once, so cost grows per room while reward stays capped at one voice per real worker. Honest agents accrue a delta of trust each epoch wherever they land, and it follows them. Spread aliases further and they only dilute; an archipelago never becomes a continent.
